sentences.zh: 顯德四年春正月己丑朔，帝御崇元殿受朝賀，仗衛如儀。

translations.literal: In spring of the fourth year of Xiande, on the first day of the first month, the day jichou, the Emperor took the Hall of Exalted Origin to receive court congratulations; guards of honor followed ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Xiande 4, on New Year's Day of the first month, the Emperor held court in the Hall of Exalted Origin to receive congratulations; guards and insignia followed the prescribed ceremony.

sentences.zh: 詔天下見禁罪人，除大辟外，一切釋放。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that throughout the realm all prisoners in custody, except those guilty of capital crimes, be released entirely.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that all prisoners held throughout the realm, except those sentenced to death, be released without exception.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，兵部尚書張昭上言：「奉詔編修太祖實錄及梁、唐二末主實錄。

translations.literal: On renyin, Minister of War Zhang Zhao submitted a memorial: "By imperial order I am compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Taizu and the veritable records of the two last rulers of Liang and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Minister of War Zhang Zhao memorialized: "By imperial order I am compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Taizu and the veritable records of the final rulers of Liang and Tang.

sentences.zh: 伏以撰《漢書》者先為項籍，編《蜀記》首序劉璋，貴神器之傳授有因，歷數之推遷得序。

translations.literal: I submit that those who compiled the 《Book of Han》 first treated Xiang Yu, and those who compiled the 《Records of Shu》 began with Liu Zhang, honoring that the transmission of the regalia has its causes and the succession of the mandate proceeds in order.
translations.idiomatic: I note that the compilers of the 《Book of Han》 began with Xiang Yu, and the 《Records of Shu》 opened with Liu Zhang, reflecting the principle that the transfer of the mandate has its logic and dynastic succession must follow proper sequence.

sentences.zh: 伏緣漢隱帝君臨在太祖之前，歷試之績，並在隱帝朝內，請先修隱帝實錄，以全太祖之事功。

translations.literal: I submit that because Emperor Yindi of Han reigned before Emperor Taizu, and his trials in office all fell within Yindi's reign, I request that the Veritable Records of Yindi be compiled first, so as to complete the achievements of Emperor Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Because Emperor Yindi of Han reigned before Taizu and his formative service all fell under Yindi, I ask that Yindi's veritable records be compiled first, so that Taizu's full career may be properly set forth.

sentences.zh: 又以唐末主之前有閔帝，在位四月，出奔於衛，亦未編紀，請修閔帝實錄。

translations.literal: Moreover, before the last Tang ruler there was Emperor Min, who reigned four months and fled to Wei; his reign too has not been recorded—I request that the Veritable Records of Emperor Min be compiled.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, before the last Tang emperor there was Emperor Min, who reigned four months and fled to Wei; no record has been made of him either, and I ask that his veritable records be compiled.

sentences.zh: 其清泰帝實錄，請書為廢帝實錄。

translations.literal: As for the Veritable Records of Emperor Qingtai, I request that they be written as the Veritable Records of the Deposed Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: As for the veritable records of Emperor Qingtai, I ask that they be titled the Veritable Records of the Deposed Emperor.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was approved.

translations.literal: Left editorial annotation bracket.
translations.idiomatic: Opening editorial annotation.

sentences.zh: （案：自「唐末主」以上，原文疑有脫誤。

translations.literal: (Note: From "the last Tang ruler" upward, the original text appears to have omissions or errors.
translations.idiomatic: (Editorial note: From the passage on "the last Tang ruler" upward, the received text appears corrupt or incomplete.

sentences.zh: 據《五代會要》云：梁末主之上有郢王友珪，篡弒居位，未有紀錄，請依《宋書》劉劭例，書為「元兇友珪」，其末主請依古義書曰後梁實錄。

translations.literal: According to the 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》: above the last Liang ruler was Prince Ying Yougui, who usurped the throne by regicide and for whom no record exists—I request that following the example of Liu Shao in the 《Book of Song》, he be written as "the arch-criminal Yougui," and that the last ruler be written according to ancient propriety as the Veritable Records of Later Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 states that before the last Liang ruler stood Prince Ying Yougui, who seized power by regicide and lacks a record; following the precedent of Liu Shao in the 《Book of Song》, he should be entered as "the arch-criminal Yougui," while the final ruler should be titled the Veritable Records of Later Liang in accordance with ancient usage.

sentences.zh: 又，唐末主之前有應順帝，在位四月出奔，亦未編紀，請書為前廢帝，清泰主為後廢帝，其書並為實錄。）〉

translations.literal: Moreover, before the last Tang ruler was Emperor Yingshun, who reigned four months and fled; he too has no compiled record—I request that he be written as the Former Deposed Emperor and the Qingtai ruler as the Later Deposed Emperor, both as veritable records.) Right editorial annotation bracket.
translations.idiomatic: Before the last Tang emperor there was also Emperor Yingshun, who reigned four months and fled without a compiled record; he should be titled the Former Deposed Emperor and the Qingtai ruler the Later Deposed Emperor, each with veritable records.) Closing editorial annotation.

sentences.zh: 丁未，淮南道招討使李重進奏，破淮賊五千人於壽州北。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Li Chongjin, Pacification Commissioner of the Huainan Circuit, reported that he had defeated five thousand Huai rebels north of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Li Chongjin, pacification commissioner of Huainan, reported defeating five thousand Southern Tang troops north of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，李景遣其弟偽齊王達率全軍來援壽州，達留駐濠州，遣其將許文縝、邊鎬、朱元領兵數萬，溯淮而上，至紫金山，設十餘寨，與城內烽火相應。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Jing had sent his younger brother, the false Prince of Qi Da, leading the full army to relieve Shouzhou; Da remained stationed at Haozhou and sent his generals Xu Wenzhen, Bian Hao, and Zhu Yuan leading tens of thousands of troops up the Huai to Purple Gold Mountain, where they established more than ten camps, coordinating beacon fires with those inside the city.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Jing had sent his brother, the pretender Prince of Qi Li Da, with the full army to relieve Shouzhou; Da held Haozhou and dispatched Xu Wenzhen, Bian Hao, and Zhu Yuan with tens of thousands of men up the Huai to Purple Gold Mountain, where they pitched more than ten camps and coordinated beacon signals with the besieged city.

sentences.zh: 又築夾道數里，將抵壽春，為運糧之路，至是為重進所敗。

translations.literal: They also built a walled corridor several li long, nearly reaching Shouchun as a route for transporting grain—at this time they were defeated by Chongjin.
translations.idiomatic: They also built a walled supply corridor several li long, nearly reaching Shouchun, but by then Chongjin had defeated them.

sentences.zh: 戊申，詔取來月幸淮南。

translations.literal: On wushen, an edict ordered that next month the Emperor would visit Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, an edict announced that the following month the Emperor would tour Huainan in person.

translations.literal: Left editorial annotation bracket.
translations.idiomatic: Opening editorial annotation.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·李蒨傳》：師老無功，時請罷兵為便，世宗令範質、王溥就蒨謀之。

translations.literal: (According to the 《History of Song·Biography of Li Gu》: the army was weary and without success; at the time many urged withdrawal as expedient; Shizong sent Fan Zhi and Wang Pu to consult with Gu.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《History of Song》, Biography of Li Gu, records that the campaign had dragged on without victory and many urged withdrawal; Shizong sent Fan Zhi and Wang Pu to consult Li Gu.

sentences.zh: 蒨手疏請親征，有必勝之利者三，世宗大悅，用其策。）〉

translations.literal: Gu wrote in his own hand urging a personal campaign, citing three advantages that assured victory; Shizong was greatly pleased and adopted his plan.) Right editorial annotation bracket.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu submitted a personal memorial urging the emperor to take the field himself, citing three reasons victory was assured; Shizong was delighted and adopted his plan.) Closing editorial annotation.

sentences.zh: 二月庚申，以前工部侍郎王敏為司農卿。

translations.literal: In the second month, on gengshen, the former Vice Minister of Works Wang Min was made Director of the Directorate of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengshen, former Vice Minister of Works Wang Min was appointed Director of the Directorate of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，詔每遇入閣日，賜百官廊下食，從舊制也。

translations.literal: On xinyou, an edict ordered that on every day of entering the inner court, officials of the hundred offices be granted food in the corridor below, following the old regulation.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, an edict restored the old practice of granting corridor meals to the full bureaucracy on days when the emperor entered the inner court.

sentences.zh: 淮南道行營都監向訓奏，破淮賊二千於黃蓍寨。

translations.literal: Xiang Xun, overall supervisor of the Huainan field headquarters, reported that he had defeated two thousand Huai rebels at Huangqi Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xun, overall supervisor of the Huainan field army, reported defeating two thousand enemy troops at Huangqi Camp.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以樞密副使王樸為權東京留守兼判開封府，以三司使張美為大內都巡檢。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wang Pu was made acting Eastern Capital regent and concurrently administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture; Commissioner of the Three Departments Zhang Mei was made chief inspector of the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs Wang Pu was made acting regent of the Eastern Capital with concurrent authority over Kaifeng, and Three Departments Commissioner Zhang Mei was appointed chief inspector of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，車駕發京師。

translations.literal: On yihai, the imperial carriage departed the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, the emperor departed the capital.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，次下蔡。

translations.literal: On yiyou, he halted at Xiaxia.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, the court halted at Xiaxia.

sentences.zh: 三月庚寅旦，帝率諸軍駐於紫金山下，命今上率親軍登山擊賊，連破數寨，斬獲數千，斷其來路，賊軍首尾不相救。

translations.literal: At dawn on gengyin in the third month, the Emperor led the armies and encamped below Purple Gold Mountain; he ordered the Present Lord to lead the personal guard up the mountain to strike the rebels, breaking several camps in succession, killing and capturing several thousand, cutting their supply route so that the rebel army head and tail could not aid each other.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on gengyin in the third month, the Emperor encamped below Purple Gold Mountain with the main army and ordered the present sovereign to lead the imperial guard up the slope; they stormed several camps in succession, killing and capturing thousands, severed the enemy line of communication, and left the rebel force unable to coordinate head and tail.

sentences.zh: 是夜，賊將朱元、朱仁裕、孫璘各舉寨來降，降其眾萬餘人。

translations.literal: That night the rebel generals Zhu Yuan, Zhu Renyu, and Sun Lin each surrendered their camps; more than ten thousand of their followers submitted.
translations.idiomatic: That night the enemy generals Zhu Yuan, Zhu Renyu, and Sun Lin surrendered their camps one after another, bringing more than ten thousand men with them.

sentences.zh: 翌日，盡陷諸寨，殺獲甚眾，擒賊大將建州節度使許文縝、前湖南節度使邊鎬，其餘黨沿流東奔，帝自率親騎沿淮北岸追賊。

translations.literal: The next day all the camps fell; kills and captures were very numerous; the great rebel generals Jianzhou military commissioner Xu Wenzhen and former Hunan military commissioner Bian Hao were captured; the rest fled east along the river, and the Emperor himself led the personal cavalry along the north bank of the Huai in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: The next day every camp was taken with heavy casualties; the enemy commanders Xu Wenzhen, military commissioner of Jianzhou, and Bian Hao, former commissioner of Hunan, were captured; the remainder fled downstream to the east, and the Emperor himself led the imperial cavalry along the north bank in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 及晡，馳二百餘里，至鎮淮軍，殺獲數千人，奪戰艦糧船數百艘，錢帛器仗不可勝數。

translations.literal: By the hour of shen they had ridden more than two hundred li and reached Zhenhuai Army, killing and capturing several thousand, seizing several hundred warships and grain boats; cash, silks, and weapons were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: By late afternoon they had ridden more than two hundred li to Zhenhuai Army, killing and capturing thousands more, seizing hundreds of warships and grain transports, and booty in cash, silk, and arms beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 甲午，詔發近縣丁夫城鎮淮軍，仍構浮梁於淮上。

translations.literal: On jiawu, an edict ordered corvée laborers from nearby counties to fortify Zhenhuai Army and also to build a pontoon bridge on the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, an edict mobilized laborers from neighboring counties to fortify Zhenhuai Army and build a pontoon bridge across the Huai.

sentences.zh: 廬州都部署劉重進奏，殺賊三千人於壽州東山口，皆紫金山之潰兵也。

translations.literal: Luzhou overall deployment commander Liu Chongjin reported that he had killed three thousand rebels at the eastern mountain pass of Shouzhou—all were routed troops from Purple Gold Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chongjin, overall deployment commander at Luzhou, reported killing three thousand enemy troops at the eastern pass of Shouzhou—all routed remnants from Purple Gold Mountain.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，授宣徽南院使、淮南節度使向訓為徐州節度使，充淮南道行營都監，即命屯鎮淮上。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Southern Bureau Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat Xiang Xun, Huainan military commissioner, was made Xuzhou military commissioner and appointed overall supervisor of the Huainan field headquarters, with orders to encamp immediately at Zhenhuai.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Xiang Xun, commissioner of the southern palace secretariat bureau and military commissioner of Huainan, was made commissioner of Xuzhou and overall supervisor of the Huainan field army, with orders to encamp at once on the Huai.

sentences.zh: 己亥，帝自鎮淮軍復幸下蔡。

translations.literal: On jihai, the Emperor returned from Zhenhuai Army to visit Xiaxia again.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, the Emperor returned from Zhenhuai Army to Xiaxia.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，賜淮南降軍許文縝、邊鎬已下萬五百人衣服錢帛有差。

translations.literal: On renyin, to the Huainan surrendered troops from Xu Wenzhen and Bian Hao downward, numbering ten thousand five hundred, clothing, cash, and silks were granted in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, the court granted graded gifts of clothing, cash, and silk to the ten thousand five hundred Huainan troops who had surrendered, from Xu Wenzhen and Bian Hao downward.

sentences.zh: 丙午，壽州劉仁贍上表乞降，帝遣閣門使張保績入城慰撫。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Liu Renshan of Shouzhou submitted a memorial begging to surrender; the Emperor sent Gate Commissioner Zhang Baoji into the city to comfort and reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Liu Renshan of Shouzhou submitted a memorial offering surrender; the Emperor sent Gate Commissioner Zhang Baoji into the city to receive him.

sentences.zh: 翌日，仁贍復令子崇讓上表請罪。

translations.literal: The next day Renshan again had his son Chongrang submit a memorial begging forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Renshan had his son Chongrang submit a further memorial begging pardon.

sentences.zh: 戊申，幸壽州城北，劉仁贍與將佐已下及兵士萬餘人出降，帝慰勞久之，恩賜有差。

translations.literal: On wushen, the Emperor visited the north of Shouzhou city; Liu Renshan with his officers downward and more than ten thousand soldiers came out to surrender; the Emperor comforted them at length and bestowed favors in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, the Emperor went to the north gate of Shouzhou; Liu Renshan, his staff, and more than ten thousand troops came out to surrender; the Emperor received them at length and granted rewards according to rank.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，詔移壽州於下蔡，以故壽州為壽春縣。

translations.literal: On gengxu, an edict ordered that Shouzhou be moved to Xiaxia and the former Shouzhou be made Shouchun County.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, an edict moved the seat of Shouzhou to Xiaxia and redesignated the old city as Shouchun County.

sentences.zh: 是日，曲赦壽州管內見禁罪人，自今月二十一日已前，凡有過犯，並從釋放。

translations.literal: That same day a partial amnesty was proclaimed for prisoners held within Shouzhou's jurisdiction: for all offenses before the twenty-first day of this month, release was granted.
translations.idiomatic: That day a partial amnesty freed all prisoners in the Shouzhou region for offenses committed before the twenty-first of the month.

sentences.zh: 應歸順職員，並與加恩。

translations.literal: Officials who had submitted in allegiance were all granted added favor.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who had submitted in allegiance were all granted additional honors.

sentences.zh: 壽州管界去城五十里內，放今年秋夏租稅。

translations.literal: Within fifty li of the city in Shouzhou's jurisdiction, the autumn and summer taxes of this year were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Within fifty li of Shouzhou, the summer and autumn taxes for the year were remitted.

sentences.zh: 自來百姓，有曾受江南文字聚集山林者，並不問罪。

translations.literal: Among the common people, any who had received documents from Jiangnan and gathered in the hills and forests would not be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners who had accepted Southern Tang documents and taken refuge in the hills were not to be prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 如有曾相傷害者，今後不得更有相仇及經官論訴。

translations.literal: If any had harmed one another, henceforth they must not again take revenge or bring suits before officials.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had injured one another were forbidden thereafter to pursue vendettas or bring suits before the courts.

sentences.zh: 自用兵已來，被擄卻骨肉者，不計遠近，並許本家識認，官中給物收贖。

translations.literal: Since the campaign began, kin seized and carried off—regardless of distance—were all permitted to be identified and reclaimed by their families, with the government supplying goods for ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Since the war began, families might identify and reclaim kidnapped kin regardless of distance, with official assistance for ransom.

sentences.zh: 曾經陣敵處所暴露骸骨，並仰收拾埋瘞。

translations.literal: Exposed bones at places where armies had clashed were all to be gathered and buried.
translations.idiomatic: Exposed bones on former battlefields were to be collected and given proper burial.

sentences.zh: 自前政令有不便於民者，委本州條例聞奏，當行厘革。

translations.literal: Prior policies inconvenient to the people were entrusted to the prefecture to set out in memorial and report; reforms would be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier measures harmful to the people were to be reported by the prefecture for revision and reform.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以偽命清淮軍節度使、檢校太尉、兼侍中劉仁贍為特進、檢校太尉、兼中書令、鄆州節度使，以右羽林統軍楊信為壽州節度使。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Liu Renshan, appointed under false credentials as military commissioner of the Qinghuai Army, acting Grand Marshal, and concurrent Palace Attendant, was made Special Advancement, acting Grand Marshal, concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and military commissioner of Yanzhou; Yang Xin, commander of the Right Yulin Guard, was made military commissioner of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Liu Renshan, formerly the Southern Tang commissioner of the Qinghuai Army with acting Grand Marshal rank and concurrent Palace Attendant title, was made Special Advancement, acting Grand Marshal, concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and commissioner of Yanzhou; Yang Xin, commander of the Right Yulin Guard, was made commissioner of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 是日，劉仁贍卒。

translations.literal: That same day Liu Renshan died.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Liu Renshan died.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以江南偽命西北面行營都監使、舒州團練使朱元為蔡州防禦使，以江南偽命文德殿使、壽州監軍使周延構為衛尉卿，以江南偽命壽州營田副使孫羽為太僕卿，以壽州節度判官鄭牧為鴻臚卿，賞歸順也。

translations.literal: On renzi, Zhu Yuan, appointed under false Jiangnan credentials as northwest field supervisor and regimental commissioner of Shuzhou, was made defender of Caizhou; Zhou Yan'gou, false Wende Hall envoy and Shouzhou army supervisor, was made Director of the Court of Imperial Studs; Sun Yu, false Shouzhou agricultural deputy, was made Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud; Zheng Mu, Shouzhou military adjutant, was made Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception—all rewards for submission.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Zhu Yuan, formerly the Southern Tang northwest field supervisor and regimental commissioner of Shuzhou, was made defender of Caizhou; Zhou Yan'gou, former Wende Hall envoy and Shouzhou army supervisor, was made Director of the Court of Imperial Studs; Sun Yu, former Shouzhou agricultural deputy, was made Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud; and Zheng Mu, Shouzhou adjutant, was made Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception, all in reward for their submission.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，追奪前許州行軍司馬韓倫在身官爵，配流沙門島。

translations.literal: On guichou, the former Xuzhou campaign marshal Han Lun was stripped of all offices and titles he still held and exiled to Liushamen Island.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Han Lun, former campaign marshal of Xuzhou, was stripped of all rank and exiled to Liushamen Island.

sentences.zh: 倫，侍衛馬軍都指揮使令坤之父也。

translations.literal: Lun was the father of Lingkun, Commander of the Palace Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was the father of Han Lingkun, commander of the Palace Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 令坤領陳州，倫在州干預郡政，掊斂之暴，公私患之，為項城民武都等所訟。

translations.literal: Lingkun held Chenzhou; Lun in the prefecture interfered in county government and extorted with violent cruelty, troubling public and private alike, and was sued by Wu Du of Xiangcheng and others.
translations.idiomatic: While Lingkun held Chenzhou, Lun meddled in local government and extorted so brutally that both officials and commoners suffered; the people of Xiangcheng, led by Wu Du, brought suit against him.

sentences.zh: 帝命殿中侍御史率汀就按之，倫詐報汀云「準詔赴闕」，汀即奏之，帝愈怒，遽令遣劾，盡得其實，故有是命。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Palace Censor Shuai Ting to investigate on the spot; Lun falsely reported to Ting that he was "proceeding to court by imperial order," and Ting memorialized this at once; the Emperor grew still angrier and immediately ordered a formal inquiry, which fully established the facts—hence this decree.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Palace Censor Shuai Ting to investigate; Lun falsely told Ting he was "proceeding to court by imperial order," and when Ting reported this the Emperor's anger deepened; he ordered a formal inquiry that confirmed every charge, leading to the decree above.

translations.literal: Left editorial annotation bracket.
translations.idiomatic: Opening editorial annotation.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·韓令坤傳》云：倫法當棄市，令坤泣請於世宗，遂免死。）〉

translations.literal: (According to the 《History of Song·Biography of Han Lingkun》: by law Lun should have been executed in the marketplace; Lingkun wept and begged Shizong, and he was spared death.) Right editorial annotation bracket.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《History of Song》, Biography of Han Lingkun, states that Lun should have been executed in the marketplace by law, but Lingkun wept and begged Shizong, and his life was spared.) Closing editorial annotation.

sentences.zh: 遣左諫議大夫尹日就於壽州開倉賑饑民。

translations.literal: Left Remonstrance Counselor Yin Ri was sent to open the granaries at Shouzhou and relieve the famine-stricken people.
translations.idiomatic: Left Remonstrance Counselor Yin Ri was sent to open the Shouzhou granaries and relieve the famine-stricken populace.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，車駕發下蔡還京。

translations.literal: On bingchen, the imperial carriage departed Xiaxia and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, the emperor left Xiaxia and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 夏四月己巳，車駕至自下蔡。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jisi, the imperial carriage arrived from Xiaxia.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jisi, the emperor arrived back from Xiaxia.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以江南偽命西北面行營應援使、前永安軍節度使、檢校太尉許文縝為左監門衛上將軍、檢校太尉，以偽命西北面行營應援都軍使、前武安軍節度使邊鎬為左千牛衛上將軍、檢校太傅。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Xu Wenzhen, appointed under false Jiangnan credentials as northwest field relief envoy and former Yong'an Army military commissioner, acting Grand Marshal, was made senior general of the Left Directorate of Gate Guards, acting Grand Marshal; Bian Hao, false northwest field relief commander and former Wu'an Army military commissioner, was made senior general of the Left Directorate of Thousand-Ox Guards, acting Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Xu Wenzhen, formerly the Southern Tang northwest relief envoy and commissioner of the Yong'an Army with acting Grand Marshal rank, was made senior general of the Left Gate Guard with acting Grand Marshal title; Bian Hao, former northwest relief commander and commissioner of the Wu'an Army, was made senior general of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard with acting Grand Mentor rank.

sentences.zh: 丙子，宰臣李穀以風痹經年，上章請退，凡三上章，不允。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Chief Minister Li Gu, afflicted with wind paralysis for years, submitted a memorial requesting retirement; he submitted three memorials in all, but none was granted.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Chief Minister Li Gu, who had suffered from rheumatism for years, submitted a memorial requesting retirement; he did so three times, but each request was denied.

translations.literal: Left editorial annotation bracket.
translations.idiomatic: Opening editorial annotation.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·李蒨傳》：蒨扶疾入見便殿，詔令不拜，命坐御座側。

translations.literal: (According to the 《History of Song·Biography of Li Gu》: Gu, supporting himself in illness, entered the side hall for audience; an edict ordered that he not bow, and he was told to sit beside the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《History of Song》, Biography of Li Gu, records that Gu came to the side hall in his illness; the emperor excused him from bowing and had him sit beside the throne.

sentences.zh: 以抱疾久，請辭相位，世宗怡然勉之，謂曰：「譬如家有四子，一人有疾，棄而不養，非父之道也。

translations.literal: Because he had long been ill he asked to resign the chancellorship; Shizong calmly encouraged him, saying: "It is like a household with four sons—if one is ill and is abandoned and not cared for, that is not a father's way.
translations.idiomatic: Having been ill so long, he asked to resign the chancellorship; Shizong gently urged him to stay, saying, "Suppose a household has four sons and one falls ill—would a father abandon him? That is not a father's way.

sentences.zh: 朕君臨萬方，卿處輔相之位，君臣之間分義斯在，奈何以祿奉為言。

translations.literal: I rule the myriad regions; you occupy the position of chief minister—the duty between ruler and minister stands thus; how can you speak in terms of salary and stipend?
translations.idiomatic: I rule the realm and you stand as chief minister—the bond between us is defined by duty, not by salary and stipend.

sentences.zh: 」穀愧謝而退。）〉

translations.literal: " Gu withdrew in shame and thanks.) Right editorial annotation bracket.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Gu withdrew in shame and gratitude.) Closing editorial annotation.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，斬內供奉官孫延希於都市，禦廚使董延勛、副使張皓、武德副使盧繼升並停職。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Inner Palace Attendant Sun Yanxi was executed in the marketplace; Imperial Kitchen Commissioner Dong Yanxun, Vice Commissioner Zhang Hao, and Wude Vice Commissioner Lu Jisheng were all suspended from office.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Inner Palace Attendant Sun Yanxi was executed in the marketplace; Imperial Kitchen Commissioner Dong Yanxun, Vice Commissioner Zhang Hao, and Wude Vice Commissioner Lu Jisheng were all removed from office.

sentences.zh: 時重修永福殿，命延希督役，上見役夫有就瓦中啖飯，以柿為匕者，大怒，斬延希而罷延勛等。

translations.literal: At the time the Yongfu Hall was being rebuilt and Yanxi was ordered to supervise the labor; the Emperor saw laborers eating from broken tiles and using persimmons as spoons, was greatly angered, executed Yanxi, and dismissed Yanxun and the others.
translations.idiomatic: While the Yongfu Hall was being rebuilt under Yanxi's supervision, the emperor saw laborers eating from broken tiles and using persimmons as spoons; enraged, he executed Yanxi and dismissed Yanxun and the others.

sentences.zh: 壬午，故彭城郡夫人劉氏追冊為皇后。

translations.literal: On renwu, the late Lady of Pengcheng Commandery, née Liu, was posthumously enfeoffed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, the late Lady Liu of Pengcheng Commandery was posthumously enfeoffed as empress.

sentences.zh: 癸未，故皇子贈左驍衛大將軍誼再贈太尉，追封越王；

translations.literal: On guiwei, the late prince posthumously granted Left General of the Valiant Cavalry Guard Yi was again granted Grand Marshal and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yue;
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, the late Prince Yi, formerly granted Left General of the Valiant Cavalry Guard, was posthumously advanced to Grand Marshal and enfeoffed as Prince of Yue;

sentences.zh: 故皇子贈左武衛大將軍誠再贈太傅，追封吳王；

translations.literal: the late prince posthumously granted Left General of the Martial Guard Cheng was again granted Grand Mentor and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Wu;
translations.idiomatic: the late Prince Cheng, formerly granted Left General of the Martial Guard, was posthumously advanced to Grand Mentor and enfeoffed as Prince of Wu;

sentences.zh: 故皇子贈左屯衛大將軍諴再贈太保，追封韓王。

translations.literal: the late prince posthumously granted Left General of the Garrison Guard Shen was again granted Grand Guardian and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: and the late Prince Shen, formerly granted Left General of the Garrison Guard, was posthumously advanced to Grand Guardian and enfeoffed as Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 故皇弟贈太保侗再贈太傅，追封郯王；

translations.literal: The late imperial younger brother posthumously granted Grand Guardian Tong was again granted Grand Mentor and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Tan;
translations.idiomatic: The late imperial brother Tong, formerly granted Grand Guardian, was posthumously advanced to Grand Mentor and enfeoffed as Prince of Tan;

sentences.zh: 故皇弟贈司空信再贈司徒，追封杞王。

translations.literal: the late imperial younger brother posthumously granted Minister of Works Xin was again granted Minister of Education and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: and the late imperial brother Xin, formerly granted Minister of Works, was posthumously advanced to Minister of Education and enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 故皇第三妹樂安公主追冊莒國長公主，故皇第五妹永寧公主追冊梁國長公主。

translations.literal: The late third imperial sister, Princess Le'an, was posthumously enfeoffed as Eldest Princess of Ju; the late fifth imperial sister, Princess Yongning, was posthumously enfeoffed as Eldest Princess of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The late third imperial sister, Princess Le'an, was posthumously enfeoffed as Eldest Princess of Ju, and the late fifth sister, Princess Yongning, as Eldest Princess of Liang.

sentences.zh: 故皇從弟贈左領軍大將軍守願再贈左衛大將軍，故皇從弟贈左監門將軍奉超再贈右衛大將軍，故皇從弟贈左千牛衛將軍愻再贈右武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: The late imperial cousin posthumously granted Left General of the Leading Army Guard Shouyuan was again granted Left General of the Imperial Guard; the late imperial cousin posthumously granted Left Gate Guard General Fengchao was again granted Right General of the Imperial Guard; the late imperial cousin posthumously granted Left Thousand-Ox Guard General Sun was again granted Right General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The late cousin Shouyuan, formerly granted Left General of the Leading Army Guard, was posthumously advanced to Left General of the Imperial Guard; the late cousin Fengchao, formerly Left Gate Guard general, to Right General of the Imperial Guard; and the late cousin Sun, formerly Left Thousand-Ox Guard general, to Right General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以先降到江南兵士團結為三十指揮，號懷德軍。

translations.literal: On jiashen, surrendered Jiangnan troops who had submitted earlier were organized into thirty commands, titled the Army of Cherished Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, earlier Jiangnan troops who had surrendered were organized into thirty commands called the Army of Cherished Virtue.

sentences.zh: 五月丁亥朔，帝御崇元殿受朝，仗衛如式。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the first day, the day dinghai, the Emperor took the Hall of Exalted Origin to receive court audience; guards of honor followed the prescribed form.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fifth month, the Emperor held court in the Hall of Exalted Origin; guards and insignia followed the prescribed ceremony.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以新修永福殿改為廣政殿。

translations.literal: On jichou, the newly rebuilt Yongfu Hall was renamed the Hall of Broad Governance.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, the newly rebuilt Yongfu Hall was renamed the Hall of Broad Governance.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以端午賜文武百僚衣服，書始也。

translations.literal: On xinmao, on the Dragon Boat Festival, clothing was granted to the civil and military officials of the hundred offices—the first time this was recorded.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, the court granted festival garments to the full civil and military bureaucracy for the Dragon Boat Festival—the first recorded instance.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，侍衛親軍都指揮使、宋州節度使、充淮南道行營都招討李重進加檢校太傅、兼侍中；

translations.literal: On guisi, Li Chongjin, Commander of the Palace Personal Guard, Songzhou military commissioner, and overall pacification commissioner of the Huainan field headquarters, was advanced to acting Grand Mentor and concurrent Palace Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Li Chongjin, commander of the Palace Personal Guard, commissioner of Songzhou, and overall pacification commissioner of Huainan, was advanced to acting Grand Mentor and concurrent Palace Attendant;

sentences.zh: 以宣徽南院使、淮南節度使向訓為徐州節度使，加檢校太尉、同平章事。

translations.literal: Xiang Xun, Southern Bureau Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat and Huainan military commissioner, was made Xuzhou military commissioner, advanced to acting Grand Marshal and Associate Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xun, southern bureau commissioner and commissioner of Huainan, was made commissioner of Xuzhou with acting Grand Marshal rank and appointment as Associate Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丙申，斬密州防禦副使侯希進於本郡。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Vice Defender of Mizhou Hou Xijin was executed in his own prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Hou Xijin, vice defender of Mizhou, was executed in his own prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時太常博士張糾檢視本州夏苗，移牒希進分檢，希進以不奉朝旨，不從。

translations.literal: At the time Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhang Jiu was inspecting the summer seedlings of the prefecture and sent a dispatch ordering Xijin to share the inspection; Xijin, claiming he had not received court orders, refused.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Zhang Jiu of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was inspecting the prefecture's summer seedlings and ordered Xijin to assist; Xijin refused on the grounds that he had received no court directive.

sentences.zh: 糾具事以聞，帝怒，遣使斬之。

translations.literal: Jiu set out the matter in full and reported it; the Emperor was angry and sent an envoy to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiu reported the full matter; the Emperor was enraged and sent an envoy to execute Xijin.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以滑州節度使兼殿前都點檢、駙馬都尉張永德為澶州節度使，加檢校太尉；

translations.literal: On dingyou, Zhang Yongde, Huazhou military commissioner, concurrent Director of the Palace Front, and Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-law, was made Chuanzhou military commissioner and advanced to acting Grand Marshal;
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Zhang Yongde, commissioner of Huazhou, Director of the Palace Front, and Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-law, was made commissioner of Chuanzhou with acting Grand Marshal rank;

sentences.zh: 以今上為滑州節度使，加檢校太保，依前殿前都指揮使。

translations.literal: the Present Lord was made Huazhou military commissioner, advanced to acting Grand Guardian, and continued as before as Director of the Palace Front.
translations.idiomatic: the present sovereign was made commissioner of Huazhou with acting Grand Guardian rank while retaining his post as Director of the Palace Front.

sentences.zh: 今上以三年十月宣授同州節度使，未於正衙宣制，至是移鎮滑臺，故自永州防禦使授焉。

translations.literal: The Present Lord had been announced and appointed Tongzhou military commissioner in the tenth month of the third year but the appointment had not been proclaimed in the main court; now he was transferred to Huatai, and therefore was appointed from his post as defender of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The present sovereign had been appointed commissioner of Tongzhou in the tenth month of Xiande 3 but the appointment had never been proclaimed in the main court; now, transferred to Huazhou, he was formally advanced from his post as defender of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 以侍衛馬軍都指揮使、洋州節度使韓令坤為陳州節度使、加檢校太傅；

translations.literal: Han Lingkun, Commander of the Palace Cavalry Guard and Yangzhou military commissioner, was made Chenzhou military commissioner and advanced to acting Grand Mentor;
translations.idiomatic: Han Lingkun, commander of the Palace Cavalry Guard and commissioner of Yangzhou, was made commissioner of Chenzhou with acting Grand Mentor rank;

sentences.zh: 以權侍衛步軍都指揮使、岳州防禦使袁彥為曹州節度使，加檢校太保，並典軍如故。

translations.literal: Yuan Yan, acting Commander of the Palace Infantry Guard and defender of Yuezhou, was made Caozhou military commissioner and advanced to acting Grand Guardian, each continuing to command his army as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yan, acting commander of the Palace Infantry Guard and defender of Yuezhou, was made commissioner of Caozhou with acting Grand Guardian rank, each retaining command of his army.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以左神武統軍劉重進為鄧州節度使，以虎捷左廂都指揮使、閬州防禦使趙晁為河陽節度使，以兗州防禦使白延遇為同州節度使。

translations.literal: On jihai, Liu Chongjin, commander of the Left Divine Martial Army, was made Dengzhou military commissioner; Zhao Chao, commander of the Left Tiger Swift Division and defender of Langzhou, was made Heyang military commissioner; Bai Yanyu, defender of Yanzhou, was made Tongzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Liu Chongjin, commander of the Left Divine Martial Army, was made commissioner of Dengzhou; Zhao Chao, commander of the Left Tiger Swift Division and defender of Langzhou, commissioner of Heyang; and Bai Yanyu, defender of Yanzhou, commissioner of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，宰臣範質、李穀、王溥並加爵邑，改功臣。

translations.literal: On xinchou, chief ministers Fan Zhi, Li Gu, and Wang Pu were all advanced in noble rank and fief, and their merit titles were changed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, chief ministers Fan Zhi, Li Gu, and Wang Pu were all advanced in noble rank and fief and given new merit titles.

sentences.zh: 樞密使魏仁浦加檢校太傅，進封開國公。

translations.literal: Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wei Renpu was advanced to acting Grand Mentor and promoted to Duke Who Opens the State.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner of Military Affairs Wei Renpu was advanced to acting Grand Mentor and enfeoffed as Duke Who Opens the State.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，知廬州行府事劉重進奏，相次殺敗賊，獲戰船三十艘。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Liu Chongjin, administrator of the Luzhou field headquarters, reported that in succession he had killed and defeated the rebels and captured thirty warships.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Liu Chongjin, administrator of the Luzhou field headquarters, reported successive victories over the enemy and the capture of thirty warships.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以宣徽北院使吳延祚為宣徽南院使，權西京留守，判河南府事。

translations.literal: On renzi, Wu Yanzuo, Northern Bureau Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, was made Southern Bureau Commissioner, acting Western Capital regent, and administrator of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Wu Yanzuo, northern bureau commissioner of the palace secretariat, was made southern bureau commissioner, acting regent of the Western Capital, and administrator of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是月，詔中書門下差官詳定格律。

translations.literal: That month an edict ordered the Secretariat-Chancellery to assign officials to examine and fix the statutes and ordinances in detail.
translations.idiomatic: That month an edict ordered the Secretariat-Chancellery to assign officials to revise the penal code in detail.

sentences.zh: 中書門下奏：「差侍御史知雜事張湜等一十人詳定。

translations.literal: The Secretariat-Chancellery memorialized: "We assign Palace Censor Zhang Shi and nine others, ten in all, to examine and fix them in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat-Chancellery reported: "We assign Palace Censor Zhang Shi and nine others—ten officials in all—to conduct the detailed revision.

sentences.zh: 候畢日，委御史臺尚書省四品已上、兩省五品已上官，參詳可否，送中書門下議定，奏取進止。

translations.literal: When the work is finished, we entrust officials of the fourth rank and above in the Censorate and Ministry of State Affairs and officials of the fifth rank and above in the two inner courts to review what is feasible, send it to the Secretariat-Chancellery for deliberation and decision, and memorialize for imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: When they finish, officials of the fourth rank and above in the Censorate and Ministry of State Affairs and fifth-rank officials of the two inner courts shall review the draft, the Secretariat-Chancellery shall deliberate, and a memorial shall be submitted for imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 六月丁巳，前濠州刺史齊藏珍以罪棄市。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on dingsi, the former prefect of Haozhou Qi Cangzhen was executed in the marketplace for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dingsi, Qi Cangzhen, former prefect of Haozhou, was executed in the marketplace for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 己未，以責授耀州司馬鐘謨為衛尉少卿，賜紫。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Zhong Mo, demoted to military adjutant of Yaozhou, was made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Studs and granted purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Zhong Mo, demoted to adjutant of Yaozhou, was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Studs and granted purple robes.

sentences.zh: 帝既誅孫晟，尋竄謨為耀州，既而悔之，故有是命。

translations.literal: The Emperor had already executed Sun Sheng and soon banished Mo to Yaozhou; he later regretted it, and therefore issued this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After executing Sun Sheng, the Emperor had banished Zhong Mo to Yaozhou; he later regretted it, which led to this appointment.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，西京奏，伊陽山谷中有金屑，民淘取之。

translations.literal: On xinyou, the Western Capital reported that in the valleys of Yiyang there were gold particles, which the people panned for.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, the Western Capital reported gold particles in the Yiyang valleys, which local people were panning.

sentences.zh: 詔勿禁。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that this not be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that the practice was not to be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，詔在朝文資官再舉堪為令、錄、從事者各一人。

translations.literal: On yiyou, an edict ordered that each civil official at court recommend one person fit to serve as magistrate, registrar, or clerk.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, an edict required each civil official at court to recommend one candidate qualified to serve as county magistrate, registrar, or clerk.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丁亥，以前徐州節度使、檢校太師、兼中書令武行德為左衛上將軍。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on dinghai, the former Xuzhou military commissioner, acting Grand Preceptor, and concurrent Director of the Secretariat Wu Xingde was made senior general of the Left Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on dinghai, former Xuzhou commissioner Wu Xingde, acting Grand Preceptor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat, was made senior general of the Left Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔行德分兵屯定遠縣，既為淮寇所襲，王師死者數百人，帝懲其僨軍之咎，故以環衛處之。

translations.literal: Earlier, an edict had ordered Xingde to divide his troops and encamp at Dingyuan County; they were then attacked by Huai rebels and several hundred of the imperial army died; the Emperor punished the fault of the defeated army and therefore placed him in the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xingde had been ordered to detach troops to garrison Dingyuan County; they were ambushed by Huai rebels and several hundred imperial soldiers died; the Emperor blamed the defeat and transferred him to a palace guard post.

sentences.zh: 以前河陽節度使李繼勛為右衛大將軍，責壽春南寨之敗也。

translations.literal: The former Heyang military commissioner Li Jixun was made Right General of the Imperial Guard, in censure for the defeat at the southern camp of Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Former Heyang commissioner Li Jixun was made Right General of the Imperial Guard, punished for the defeat at Shouchun's southern camp.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以刑部尚書王易為太子少保致仕，以右監門衛上將軍蓋萬為左衛上將軍致仕。

translations.literal: On renchen, Minister of Justice Wang Yi was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and retired; Gai Wan, senior general of the Right Gate Guard, was made senior general of the Left Imperial Guard and retired.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Minister of Justice Wang Yi retired as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Gai Wan, senior general of the Right Gate Guard, retired as senior general of the Left Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 己酉，司農卿王敏卒。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Director of the Directorate of Agriculture Wang Min died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Director of the Directorate of Agriculture Wang Min died.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，詔曰：「準令，諸論田宅婚姻，起十一月一日至三月三十日止者。

translations.literal: On jiachen, an edict stated: "According to statute, all suits over fields, houses, and marriage that begin from the first day of the eleventh month through the thirtieth day of the third month are suspended.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, an edict stated: "By statute, suits over land, houses, and marriage filed between the first day of the eleventh month and the thirtieth day of the third month are suspended.

sentences.zh: 州縣爭論，舊有厘革，每至農月，貴塞訟端。

translations.literal: Disputes in prefectures and counties had long been reformed in this way; each year when farming season arrived, it was prized to block the flood of litigation.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county disputes had long been regulated thus, closing the courts during the farming season to stem litigation.

sentences.zh: 近聞官吏因循，由此成弊，凡有訴競，故作逗遛，至時而不與盡辭，入務而即便停罷，強猾者因茲得計，孤弱者無以自伸。

translations.literal: Recently it was heard that officials were lax and indulgent, and from this an abuse arose: whenever there was litigation they deliberately delayed, not completing the case when the season arrived, and stopping work as soon as court reopened; the strong and cunning profited thereby, while the isolated and weak had no means to vindicate themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Recently officials had grown lax, creating an abuse: they deliberately delayed suits, refusing to finish cases before the suspension date and halting work as soon as court reopened; the powerful exploited the delay while the weak could not obtain justice.

sentences.zh: 起今後應有人論訴陳詞狀，至二月三十日權停。

translations.literal: Henceforth, whenever anyone files a petition of suit or complaint, it shall be provisionally suspended until the thirtieth day of the second month.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth all new petitions and complaints shall be provisionally suspended until the thirtieth day of the second month.

sentences.zh: 若是交相侵奪、情理妨害、不可停滯者，不拘此限」。

translations.literal: If there is mutual seizure and encroachment, or circumstances of harm that cannot be delayed, this limit does not apply."
translations.idiomatic: Cases involving mutual seizure or urgent harm that cannot be delayed are not subject to this limit."

sentences.zh: 八月乙卯朔，兵部尚書張昭上疏，望準唐朝故事，置制舉以罩英才。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the first day, the day yimao, Minister of War Zhang Zhao submitted a memorial, hoping that following Tang dynasty precedent, special examinations might be established to gather outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eighth month, Minister of War Zhang Zhao memorialized that, following Tang precedent, special examinations should be established to gather outstanding talent.

sentences.zh: 帝覽而善之，因命昭具制舉合行事件，條奏以聞。

translations.literal: The Emperor read it and approved; he therefore ordered Zhao to set out in detail the matters appropriate for the special examinations and memorialize them item by item.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved the proposal and ordered Zhao to draft the full regulations for the examinations and submit them item by item.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以太常卿田敏為工部尚書，以太子賓客司徒詡為太常卿。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Tian Min was made Minister of Works; Guest of the Heir Apparent Situ Xu was made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Tian Min was made Minister of Works, and Guest of the Heir Apparent Situ Xu was made director of that court.

sentences.zh: 辛未，詔在朝武班，各舉武勇膽力堪為軍職者一人。

translations.literal: On xinwei, an edict ordered that each military official at court recommend one person of martial courage and daring fit for military office.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, an edict required each military official at court to recommend one candidate of proven courage fit for military service.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，賜左監門上將軍許文縝、右千牛上將軍邊鎬、右衛大將軍王環、衛尉卿周延構、太府卿馮延魯、太僕卿鄭牧、鴻臚卿孫羽、衛尉少卿鐘謨、工部郎中何幼沖各冬服絹二百匹、綿五百兩。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, to Xu Wenzhen, senior general of the Left Gate Guard; Bian Hao, senior general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard; Wang Huan, Right General of the Imperial Guard; Zhou Yan'gou, Director of the Court of Imperial Studs; Feng Yanlu, Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury; Zheng Mu, Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud; Sun Yu, Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception; Zhong Mo, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Studs; and He Youchong, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works—each was granted two hundred bolts of silk for winter garments and five hundred taels of cotton.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Xu Wenzhen, Bian Hao, Wang Huan, Zhou Yan'gou, Feng Yanlu, Zheng Mu, Sun Yu, Zhong Mo, and He Youchong of the Ministry of Works were each granted two hundred bolts of winter silk and five hundred taels of cotton.

sentences.zh: 文縝已下，皆吳、蜀之士也。

translations.literal: From Wenzhen downward, all were men of Wu and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: From Xu Wenzhen downward, all were former subjects of Wu and Shu.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，宰臣李穀罷相，守司空，加食邑實封。

translations.literal: On yihai, Chief Minister Li Gu left the chancellorship, retained the post of Minister of Works, and was granted added noble fief and substantive enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Chief Minister Li Gu resigned the chancellorship, retained the rank of Minister of Works, and received an enlarged noble fief with substantive enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 穀抱疾周歲，累上表求退，至是方允其請。

translations.literal: Gu had been ill for a full year and repeatedly submitted memorials requesting retirement; only now was his request granted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu had been ill for a full year and had repeatedly asked to retire; only now was his request granted.

sentences.zh: 以樞密副使、戶部侍郎王樸為樞密使、檢校太保。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Vice Minister of Revenue Wang Pu was made Commissioner of Military Affairs and acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs and Vice Minister of Revenue Wang Pu was made commissioner of military affairs with acting Grand Guardian rank.

sentences.zh: 癸未，前濮州刺史胡立自偽蜀回，蜀主孟昶寓書於帝，其末云：昶昔在齠齔，即離並都，亦承皇帝鳳起晉陽，龍興汾水，合敘鄉關之分，以陳玉帛之歡。

translations.literal: On guiwei, the former prefect of Puzhou Hu Li returned from false Shu; the Shu ruler Meng Chang sent a letter to the Emperor, its close reading: "Chang, while still in infancy, left Bingdu; I also know that Your Majesty rose like a phoenix at Jinyang and ascended like a dragon on the Fen River—we should renew our ties as fellow townsmen and exchange the courtesies of jade and silk.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, former Puzhou prefect Hu Li returned from Shu; Shu ruler Meng Chang sent a letter to the Emperor ending with: "While still a child I left Taiyuan; I know Your Majesty rose like a phoenix at Jinyang and like a dragon on the Fen—we should renew our ties as fellow townsmen and exchange the courtesies due between states.

sentences.zh: 儻蒙惠以嘉音，佇望專馳信使，謹因胡立行次，聊陳感謝披述」云。

translations.literal: If I may receive your gracious reply, I earnestly await a dedicated envoy; I take the occasion of Hu Li's journey to offer these words of gratitude and explanation."
translations.idiomatic: If I may receive a gracious reply, I earnestly await a dedicated envoy; I take the occasion of Hu Li's journey to offer these words of gratitude."

sentences.zh: 初，王師之伐秦、鳳也，以立為排陣使，既而為蜀所擒。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the imperial army attacked Qin and Feng, Li was made battle-array commissioner, but was then captured by Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the campaign against Qin and Feng, Li had served as battle-array commissioner before being captured by Shu.

sentences.zh: 及秦、鳳平，得降軍數千人，其後帝念其懷土，悉放歸蜀，至是蜀人知感，故歸立於我。

translations.literal: When Qin and Feng were pacified, several thousand surrendered troops were taken; later the Emperor, mindful of their longing for home, released them all back to Shu; now the Shu people knew gratitude and therefore sent Li back to us.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin and Feng were pacified, several thousand surrendered troops were taken; the Emperor later released them all to Shu out of sympathy for their homesickness; now, moved by that kindness, the Shu sent Li back.

sentences.zh: 昶本生於太原，故其書意願與帝推鄉里之分，帝怒其抗禮，不答。

translations.literal: Chang was born in Taiyuan; therefore in his letter he wished to claim fellow-townsmen's ties with the Emperor; the Emperor was angry at his presumptuous tone and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Chang had been born in Taiyuan and therefore treated the Emperor as a fellow townsman in his letter; the Emperor was angered by the presumptuous tone and did not reply.

sentences.zh: 九月甲申朔，宰臣王溥、樞密使王樸皆丁內艱，並起復舊位。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the first day, the day jiashen, Chief Minister Wang Pu and Commissioner of Military Affairs Wang Pu both entered mourning for a parent in the inner family, and both were recalled to their former posts.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the ninth month, Chief Minister Wang Pu and Commissioner of Military Affairs Wang Pu both entered mourning for close kin and were both recalled to their former posts.

sentences.zh: 以侍衛馬步軍都指揮使、宋州節度使李重進為鄆州節度使，典軍如故。

translations.literal: Li Chongjin, Commander of the Palace Horse and Foot Guard and Songzhou military commissioner, was made Yanzhou military commissioner, continuing to command his army as before.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongjin, commander of the Palace Horse and Foot Guard and commissioner of Songzhou, was made commissioner of Yanzhou while retaining command of his army.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以前翰林學士、禮部侍郎竇儀為端明殿學士，依前禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: On jichou, the former Hanlin Academician and Vice Minister of Rites Dou Yi was made Academician of the Hall of Clear Brilliance, remaining Vice Minister of Rites as before.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, former Hanlin Academician and Vice Minister of Rites Dou Yi was made Academician of the Hall of Clear Brilliance while retaining his post as vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丙辰，賜京城內新修四寺額，以天清、天壽、顯靜、顯寧為名。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on bingchen, plaques were granted to four newly built monasteries within the capital, named Heavenly Clarity, Heavenly Longevity, Manifest Serenity, and Manifest Tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on bingchen, four newly built monasteries in the capital received plaques naming them Heavenly Clarity, Heavenly Longevity, Manifest Serenity, and Manifest Tranquility.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，左藏庫使符令光棄市。

translations.literal: On renxu, Fu Lingguang, commissioner of the Left Treasury, was executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Fu Lingguang, commissioner of the Left Treasury, was executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 時帝再議南征，先期敕令光廣造軍士袍襦，不即辦集，帝怒，命斬之。

translations.literal: At the time the Emperor was again planning a southern campaign and had beforehand ordered Lingguang to manufacture soldiers' robes and jackets on a large scale; they were not promptly assembled; the Emperor was angry and ordered his execution.
translations.idiomatic: As the Emperor was again planning a southern campaign, he had ordered Lingguang to manufacture soldiers' uniforms in quantity; when they were not ready on time, the Emperor ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 時宰臣等至庭救解，帝起入宮，遂戮於都市。

translations.literal: The chief ministers and others came to the court to plead for him, but the Emperor rose and entered the palace; Lingguang was then killed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers pleaded for him at court, but the Emperor rose and entered the palace; Lingguang was then executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 令光出勛閥之後，歷職內庭，以清慎自守，累總繁劇，甚有廉幹之譽。

translations.literal: Lingguang came from a family of meritorious nobles, had long served in the inner court, kept himself with purity and caution, repeatedly held heavy and complex duties, and enjoyed a great reputation for integrity and competence.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant of a meritorious house, Lingguang had long served in the inner court with scrupulous integrity, repeatedly held demanding posts, and enjoyed a reputation for probity and efficiency.

sentences.zh: 帝素重其為人，每加委用，至是以小過見誅，人皆冤之。

translations.literal: The Emperor had always valued his character and repeatedly entrusted him; now he was executed for a small fault, and all regarded it as unjust.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had always valued him and repeatedly entrusted him with important duties; his execution for a minor lapse was widely regarded as unjust.

sentences.zh: 戊午，詔懸制科凡三，其一曰賢良方正能直言極諫科，其二曰經學優深可為師法科，其三曰詳閑吏理達於教化科。

translations.literal: On wuwu, an edict proclaimed three special examination subjects: first, the subject of Worthy and Upright Persons Able to Speak Bluntly and Remonstrate Forcefully; second, the subject of Classical Learning Profound Enough to Serve as a Model for Teachers; third, the subject of Mastery of Administrative Principles and Understanding of Civilizing Transformation.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, an edict proclaimed three special examinations: Worthy and Upright Persons Able to Speak Bluntly and Remonstrate Forcefully; Classical Learning Profound Enough to Serve as a Model for Teachers; and Mastery of Administrative Principles and Understanding of Civilizing Transformation.

sentences.zh: 不限前資、見任職官，黃衣草澤，並許應詔。

translations.literal: Without limit on prior rank, current officeholders, or commoners in plain dress, all were permitted to answer the imperial call.
translations.idiomatic: Without restriction by prior rank, current office, or commoner status, all were permitted to compete.

sentences.zh: 時兵部尚書張昭條奏，請興制舉，故有是命。

translations.literal: At the time Minister of War Zhang Zhao had memorialized item by item requesting the establishment of special examinations, and therefore this decree was issued.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Zhang Zhao had memorialized requesting the restoration of special examinations, which led to this decree.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，河東偽命麟州刺史楊重訓以城歸順，授重訓本州防禦使、檢校太傅。

translations.literal: On guihai, Yang Chongxun of Linzhou in Hedong, appointed under false credentials, surrendered his city in submission; Chongxun was made defender of his prefecture and acting Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Yang Chongxun, the Southern Tang-appointed prefect of Linzhou in Hedong, surrendered his city; he was made defender of Linzhou with acting Grand Mentor rank.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，詔取月內車駕暫幸淮上。

translations.literal: On wuchen, an edict ordered that within the month the imperial carriage would temporarily visit the Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, an edict announced that within the month the emperor would temporarily tour the Huai region.

sentences.zh: 己巳，以樞密使王樸為權東京留守，以三司使張美為大內都點檢。

translations.literal: On jisi, Commissioner of Military Affairs Wang Pu was made acting Eastern Capital regent; Commissioner of the Three Departments Zhang Mei was made chief inspector of the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Commissioner of Military Affairs Wang Pu was made acting regent of the Eastern Capital, and Three Departments Commissioner Zhang Mei was appointed chief inspector of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 壬申，駕發京師。

translations.literal: On renshen, the imperial carriage departed the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, the emperor departed the capital.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以前鄆州節度使郭從義為徐州節度使，以徐州節度使向訓為宋州節度使。

translations.literal: On renwu, the former Yanzhou military commissioner Guo Congyi was made Xuzhou military commissioner; Xuzhou military commissioner Xiang Xun was made Songzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, former Yanzhou commissioner Guo Congyi was made commissioner of Xuzhou, and Xuzhou commissioner Xiang Xun was made commissioner of Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月癸未朔，以內客省使昝居潤為宣徽北院使，權東京留守。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the first day, the day guiwei, Inner Reception Commissioner Zan Jurun was made Northern Bureau Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat and acting Eastern Capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eleventh month, Inner Reception Commissioner Zan Jurun was made northern bureau commissioner of the palace secretariat and acting regent of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，車駕至濠州城下。

translations.literal: On bingxu, the imperial carriage reached below the walls of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, the emperor reached Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 戊子，親破十八里灘。

translations.literal: On wuzi, he personally broke the Eighteen-Li Shoals camp.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, he personally stormed the Eighteen-Li Shoals camp.

sentences.zh: 寨在濠州東北淮水之中，四面阻水，上令甲土數百人跨駝以濟。

translations.literal: The camp lay in the Huai northeast of Haozhou, blocked by water on all sides; the Emperor ordered several hundred armored soldiers to cross mounted on camels.
translations.idiomatic: The camp lay in the Huai northeast of Haozhou, surrounded by water on all sides; the Emperor ordered several hundred armored men to cross mounted on camels.

sentences.zh: 今上以騎軍浮水而渡，遂破其寨，擄其戰艦而回。

translations.literal: The Present Lord led the cavalry across floating on the water, broke the camp, captured their warships, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The present sovereign led the cavalry across the water, stormed the camp, captured the enemy warships, and returned.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，帝親率諸軍攻濠州，奪關城，破水寨，賊眾大敗，焚戰艦七十餘艘，斬首二千級，進軍攻羊馬城。

translations.literal: On guisi, the Emperor personally led the armies to attack Haozhou, seized the barrier city, broke the water camp, and the rebels were greatly defeated; more than seventy warships were burned, two thousand heads were taken, and the army advanced to attack the Sheep-and-Horse City.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, the Emperor personally led the armies against Haozhou, took the outer barrier, broke the water camp, and routed the enemy; more than seventy warships were burned, two thousand heads taken, and the army advanced against the Sheep-and-Horse redoubt.

sentences.zh: 丙申夜，偽濠州團練使郭廷謂上表陳情，且言家在江南，欲遣人稟命於李景，從之。

translations.literal: On the night of bingshen, the false Haozhou regimental commissioner Guo Tingyu submitted a memorial stating his case and saying his family was in Jiangnan; he wished to send someone to report to Li Jing for orders—this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of bingshen, the Southern Tang regimental commissioner of Haozhou Guo Tingyu submitted a memorial explaining that his family remained in Jiangnan and asking permission to send envoys to Li Jing; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，帝自濠州率大軍水陸齊進，循淮而下，命今上率精騎為前鋒。

translations.literal: On xinchou, the Emperor from Haozhou led the great army forward by land and water together, proceeding down the Huai, and ordered the Present Lord to lead elite cavalry as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, the Emperor led the main army by land and water down the Huai from Haozhou and ordered the present sovereign to lead the elite cavalry as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，大破淮賊於渦口，斬首五千級，收降卒二千餘人，奪戰船三百艘，遂鼓行而東，以追奔寇，晝夜不息，沿淮城柵，所至皆下。

translations.literal: On guimao, the Huai rebels were greatly defeated at Wokou; five thousand heads were taken, more than two thousand surrendered soldiers received, and three hundred warships seized; then with drums beating the army marched east in pursuit of the fleeing enemy without pause day or night; along the Huai every walled camp was taken as they came to it.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, the army routed the Huai rebels at Wokou, taking five thousand heads, accepting more than two thousand surrendering troops, and seizing three hundred warships; then, drums beating, it pressed east in relentless pursuit; every fortified post along the Huai fell as the army advanced.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，至泗州。

translations.literal: On yisi, they reached Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, the army reached Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 今上乘勢麾軍，焚郭門，奪月城，帝親冒矢石以攻其壘。

translations.literal: The Present Lord seized the momentum to command the army, burned the outer gate, and took the moon-wall city; the Emperor personally braved arrows and stones to assault the fortress.
translations.idiomatic: The present sovereign pressed the attack, burned the outer gate, and seized the moon-wall; the Emperor himself braved arrows and stones to assault the main fortress.

sentences.zh: 丙午，日南至，從臣拜賀於月城之上。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the winter solstice arrived; attending officials offered congratulations atop the moon-wall.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, the winter solstice, the emperor's attendants offered congratulations atop the moon-wall.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙卯，泗州守將範再遇以其城降，授再遇宿州團練使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yimao, Fan Zaiyu, defender of Sizhou, surrendered his city; Zaiyu was made regimental commissioner of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yimao, Fan Zaiyu, defender of Sizhou, surrendered the city and was made regimental commissioner of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊午，帝自泗州率眾東下，命今上領兵行於南岸，與帝夾淮而進。

translations.literal: On wuwu, the Emperor from Sizhou led the host eastward and ordered the Present Lord to lead troops along the south bank, advancing with the Emperor on opposite sides of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, the Emperor led the army east from Sizhou and ordered the present sovereign to advance along the south bank while the main force pressed down the north bank of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 己未，至清口，追及淮賊，軍行鼓噪之聲聞數十里。

translations.literal: On jiwei, they reached Qingkou, overtook the Huai rebels, and the sound of marching drums and shouts was heard for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, they reached Qingkou, overtook the Huai rebels, and the sound of drums and battle cries carried for tens of li.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，至楚州西北，大破賊眾，水陸俱奔，有賊船數艘，順流而逸，帝率驍騎與今上追之數十里，今上擒賊大將偽保義軍節度使、江北都應援使陳承昭以獻。

translations.literal: On xinyou, they reached the northwest of Chuzhou and greatly defeated the rebel host; both land and water forces fled; several rebel ships escaped downstream; the Emperor led elite cavalry with the Present Lord in pursuit for several tens of li; the Present Lord captured the great rebel general, false Baoyi Army military commissioner and north-of-the-river overall relief envoy Chen Chengzhao, and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, northwest of Chuzhou, the army routed the enemy on land and water; several enemy ships fled downstream; the Emperor and the present sovereign pursued for tens of li with elite cavalry, and the present sovereign captured the enemy commander Chen Chengzhao, false commissioner of the Baoyi Army and overall relief envoy north of the river, and presented him to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 收獲舟船，除焚蕩外得三百餘艘，將士除殺溺外得七千餘人。

translations.literal: Warships captured, apart from those burned, numbered more than three hundred; soldiers and officers captured, apart from those killed or drowned, numbered more than seven thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from those burned, more than three hundred ships were captured; apart from those killed or drowned, more than seven thousand enemy troops were taken.

sentences.zh: 初，帝之渡淮也，比無水戰之備，每遇賊之戰棹，無如之何，敵人亦以此自恃，有輕我之意。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor crossed the Huai, hitherto there had been no preparation for naval warfare; whenever they met the rebels' war boats they were at a loss, and the enemy also relied on this and held us in light esteem.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor first crossed the Huai, the army had no naval capability and could do nothing against enemy warships; the enemy took advantage of this and held the Zhou forces in contempt.

sentences.zh: 帝即於京師大集工徒，修成艛艦，逾歲得數百艘，兼得江、淮舟船，遂令所獲南軍教北人習水戰出沒之勢，未幾，舟師大備。

translations.literal: The Emperor then at the capital gathered craftsmen on a great scale and built tower ships; within a year he obtained several hundred vessels, and also acquired Yangtze and Huai boats; he then ordered captured southern troops to teach northerners the tactics of naval combat and maneuver; before long the fleet was fully prepared.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then mobilized craftsmen in the capital to build tower ships; within a year he had several hundred vessels, supplemented by Yangtze and Huai craft, and had captured southern troops train northerners in naval tactics; soon the fleet was fully ready.

sentences.zh: 至是水陸皆捷，故江南大震。

translations.literal: At this point victories came on both land and water, and therefore Jiangnan was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Victories on land and water now followed in succession, throwing Jiangnan into alarm.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，偽命濠州團練使郭廷謂以城歸順。

translations.literal: On renxu, Guo Tingyu, false Haozhou regimental commissioner, surrendered his city in submission.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Guo Tingyu, the Southern Tang regimental commissioner of Haozhou, surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，雄武軍使崔萬迪以漣水歸順。

translations.literal: On yichou, Cui Wandi, commissioner of the Xiongwu Army, surrendered Lianshui in submission.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Cui Wandi, commissioner of the Xiongwu Army, surrendered Lianshui.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以郭廷謂為亳州防禦使，

translations.literal: On bingyin, Guo Tingyu was made defender of Bozhou,
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Guo Tingyu was made defender of Bozhou,

translations.literal: Left editorial annotation bracket.
translations.idiomatic: Opening editorial annotation.

sentences.zh: （《隆平集》：廷謂望金陵大慟，再拜，然後以城降。

translations.literal: (According to the Longping Collection: Tingyu looked toward Jinling and wept bitterly, bowed twice, and then surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: (The Longping Collection records that Tingyu looked toward Jinling and wept bitterly, bowed twice, and then surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 世宗曰：「江南諸將，惟卿斷渦口僑，破定遠寨，足以報李景祿矣。

translations.literal: Shizong said: "Among the generals of Jiangnan, only you cut off the Wokou bridgehead and broke the Dingyuan camp—enough to repay the salary Li Jing gave you.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong said, "Among Jiangnan's generals, only you severed the Wokou bridgehead and broke the Dingyuan camp—enough to repay what Li Jing paid you.

sentences.zh: 濠上使李景自守，亦何能為！

translations.literal: Let Li Jing hold Haoshang himself—what can he do!"
translations.idiomatic: If Li Jing holds the Huai line himself, what can he do!"

sentences.zh: 」乃授以亳州防禦使。）〉

translations.literal: " He then appointed him defender of Bozhou.) Right editorial annotation bracket.
translations.idiomatic: " He then appointed him defender of Bozhou.) Closing editorial annotation.

sentences.zh: 以偽命濠州兵馬都監陳遷為沂州團練使，以偽命保義軍節度使陳承昭為右監門上將軍。

translations.literal: Chen Qian, false Haozhou army supervisor, was made regimental commissioner of Yizhou; Chen Chengzhao, false Baoyi Army military commissioner, was made senior general of the Right Gate Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qian, the Southern Tang army supervisor of Haozhou, was made regimental commissioner of Yizhou, and Chen Chengzhao, former commissioner of the Baoyi Army, was made senior general of the Right Gate Guard.

sentences.zh: 江南李景遣兵驅擄揚州士庶渡江，焚其州郭而去。

translations.literal: Li Jing of Jiangnan sent troops to drive and seize the officials and commoners of Yangzhou across the river, burned the prefectural walls, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing of Jiangnan sent troops to drive Yangzhou's population across the river, burned the city, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 丙子，故同州節度使白延遇贈太尉，故濠州刺史唐景思贈武清軍節度使。

translations.literal: On bingzi, the late Tongzhou military commissioner Bai Yanyu was posthumously granted Grand Marshal; the late Haozhou prefect Tang Jingsi was posthumously granted military commissioner of the Wuqing Army.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, the late commissioner of Tongzhou Bai Yanyu was posthumously granted Grand Marshal, and the late prefect of Haozhou Tang Jingsi was posthumously granted military commissioner of the Wuqing Army.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，泰州平。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Taizhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Taizhou was pacified.
